Ferris goes to the harbor

By Ana Souza

The crab mascot of the Rust project spent the morning at the harbor, counting boats and checking that every rope had exactly one owner. Sailors said the inspection was strict but fair, and that no knot was left dangling after the crab had passed.

In the afternoon Ferris met the harbor master to discuss lifetimes: how long each ship may stay at the dock, and who is responsible for moving it out before the next one arrives. The rules were written down on a large board next to the lighthouse so that every captain could read them.

What happens next

The harbor plans to publish a guide for new captains next spring. It will cover borrowing a berth for a single night, sharing a berth between two small boats, and the procedure for handing over a ship to a new owner without a gap in responsibility.
